correctness.rationale: If top-two score pair fails JR, a jointly unrepresented group U of size at least n/2 and rival supported on U force n even, every involved score exactly n/2, two identical complementary-support masks and one rival mask, and no score above n/2. Conditional on r half-score candidates their masks are iid uniform over M=binom(n,n/2) half masks; each complementary pair permits occupancy (x,0),(0,y),(1,1), with EGF 2e^z-1+z^2. Coefficient extraction produces the exact formula; for m=3 the three choices times M masks give 3M[p(1-p)]^(3n/2), and uniform tie-break gives 1/3. For fixed even n, a positive probability of every half mask yields conditional bad-event probability tending to one, so P~q^m. Independent exhaustive profiles for (2,3),(2,4),(3,3),(4,3),(4,4) agree with exact occupancy coefficients; all n,m follow analytically.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The earlier JR theorem guarantees a good maximizing tie-break; it neither asserts all ties good nor counts the bad maximizing ones. AJR and other stochastic approval results concern different axioms, events or committees; no covering all-(n,m,p) probability theorem was identified.

value.rationale: A natural adversarial-tie event in justified representation is quantified for every electorate and candidate count, not merely a small witness. The complementary-mask occupancy EGF, exact three-candidate tie-break law, and fixed-electorate many-candidate scaling supply independently useful distributional information for random approval cultures.

limitations: Independent homogeneous Bernoulli pair approvals; event is existence of at least one bad maximizing 2-committee. Only m=3 obtains uniform random tie-break failure explicitly; fixed-n m->infinity is not a joint limit.
